hypotheses.reasoning: At 20:34:56 Postgres reported transaction 98979 from payment-svc-reconciler sitting idle in transaction while holding RowExclusiveLock on "orders" (#104). Checkouts were healthy (200s in about 100ms) until then. After that, payment-svc UPDATEs on orders waited on ShareLock for that transaction (#113, #119) and were cancelled at the 10s statement timeout (#117, #127). As a result order-service's PaymentClient.charge calls timed out after 15s (#118, #128), its HTTP pool to payment-svc filled up (50/50, #133; checkout timeouts #142), and the gateway returned 504s (#134 onward). No deploy appears in the window. Redis and order-consumer look normal.

Another way to read the same lines: the problem is row-lock contention on the orders table, plus the payment-svc pool filling up. But the pool filling up is a downstream effect of the lock wait, not the origin.

verdict.recommendedAction: End the idle-in-transaction backend for transaction 98979 (payment-svc-reconciler), e.g. with pg_terminate_backend. Then fix the reconciler so it always commits or rolls back. Set idle_in_transaction_session_timeout and a lock_timeout on the reconciler's role. Finally, check that the order-service pool to payment-svc drains and gateway 504s stop.
